newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA says abortion drug safe and "approvable".
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA says abortion drug safe and "approvable".

text.p: The RU 486 abortion pill got a tentative seal of approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration on Wednesday, a significant step toward making it available to American women, the New York-based Population Council said.

The FDA deemed the drug "approvable," meaning it is safe and effective, but the Population Council must meet some additional requirements on labeling and manufucturing before it gets final FDA approval and doctors can start prescribing it, the nonprofit council said in a statement.

RU 486, which causes abortion by inducing uterine contractions, gives women an alternative to surgical abortion during the first seven weeks of pregnancy. It is made by Roussel Uclaf Co. of France and is available in several European nations.

Roussel, under pressure from the anti-abortion rights movement, did not bring the drug to the U.S. market. Instead, in an unconventional move, it gave the U.S. patent rights to the Population Council, which ran clinical tests last year.

The council did not provide details of the FDA conditions, but the drug must be administered by a physician trained in the two-step process of combining RU 486, known in the United States as mifepristone, with a second drug, misoprostol.

The FDA told the group clinical tests had shown "the safety and efficacy" of the abortion pill when used under medical supervision. The data came from two French trials involving 2,480 women and U.S. trials with more than 2,000 women, the FDA said.
"We are sure we will be able to provide the FDA the outstanding information necessary for approval," the Population Council said, adding it was "delighted" by the federal agency's decision.

RU 486 was expected by activists on both sides to transform the divisive political and emotional abortion debate in America. It can be adminstered in a physician's office, making the act of having an abortion more private and allowing patients and doctors to avoid the pickets, protests and occasional violence that have surrounded many U.S. clinics.

Doctors perform 1.5 million abortions each year in the United States. Anti-abortion forces threatened boycotts or reprisals against the French company, its U.S. subsidiaries and its parent, Germany's Hoechst AG, over the abortion pill.

In July an FDA advisory panel recommended approving RU 486 but expressed concern about labeling and the proper training of doctors administering it. Anti-abortion groups campaigned hard against the pill, saying no drug that destroys a fetus can be considered safe and the long-term effects on women's health have not been adequately studied.

Last week Planned Parenthood said in New York it received FDA clearance for its own studies of early medical abortions. Another group, New York-based Abortion Rights Mobilization, announced plans to test a cloned version of RU 486.
